description.narrative: Insatsen ska svara upp mot några av de många utmaningar media och yttrandefriheten står inför i Palestina. International Media Support (IMS) har lämnat in en ansökan till Sida om stöd till IMS Programme Strategy 2022-2024 för Palestina om 36 MSEK (12 MSEK per år 2022-2024). Programmet i Palestina är nära kopplat till IMS Menaprogram (2022-2025) vilket betyder att personal och resurser kan delas i implementeringen. Det föreslagna programmet har bedömts relevant av Sida och insatsen skulle utgöra en fortsättning av ett pågående partnerskap som bygger på tillit och ömsesidig förståelse av en vision att öka ansvarsutkrävande i Palestina över tid, genom ett stärkt civilsamhälle, oberoende media och mer professionella journalister. Insatsen kompletterar andra i portföljen inom mänskliga rättigheter-omårdet, men verkar även kompletterande till det överbryggande stödet till Palestina. IMS huvudsyfte av landstrategin för oPt (Occcupied Palestinian Territory) för 2022-2024 fokuserar på stärkande av partners och andra intressenter/aktörers möjligheter att utöva sin rätt tilll yttrandefrihet på ett ansvarsfullt, inkluderande och diversifierat sätt för att kunna förse medborgarna med påligligt innehåll och information av allmänintresse (med särskilt fokus på östra Jerusalem, område C och Gazaremsan). Under detta övergripande mål finns ett effektmål (impact objective): - Tillgång till innehåll av allmänintresse publiceras av pålitlig media som täcker, sociala, politiska och kulturella ämnen och som verkar för ansvarstagande och ansvarskrävande och människors möjligheter att utöva sina mänskliga rättigheter. Tre resultat: Resultat 1: Större delen av media intressenter/samhället är stärkta och ges möjlighet att producera etiskt, inkluderande och potentiellt livskraftigt innehåll av allmänintresse som publiken litar på och som civilsamhällesorganisationer använder. Resultat 2: Journalisters säkerhet online ökar och deras rättigheter är skyddade i domstol och genom dokumentation av brott mot pressfriheten. Resultat 3: Media stödjer organisationer och civilsamhällesorganisationer lobbar framgångsrikt för lagar som garanerar yttrandefriheten och adresserar desinformation och hatpropaganda.

To respond to some of the many challenges to media and freedom of expression in Palestine. International Media Support (IMS) has submitted a proposal to Sida to fund the IMS programme Strategy 2022-2024 for the Occupied Palestinian Territory with 36 MSEK (12m SEK annually 2022-2024). The Palestine programme is closely linked to the IMS Mena programme (2022-2025) which means it draws on staff and resources for implementation. The proposed programme has been assessed by Sida as relevant and the contribution would be a continuation of an ongoing partnership which is built upon trust and mutual understanding of a long-term vision to enhance accountability in Palestine through an enhanced civil society, independent media and more professional journalists. It is complementary to other contributions in the portfolio within the field of human rights, but also complementary to the overall support to Palestine.
IMS’ main objective of the oPt country strategy for 2022-2024 is focused on enhancing partners’ and other stakeholders’ abilities to exercise their right to freedom of expression in a responsible, inclusive and diverse manner so that they can provide citizens with reliable public interest content and information (with a specific focus on East-Jerusalem, Area C, and the Gaza Strip). Under this overarching objective there is an impact objective: -Access to public interest content published by trusted media which covers social, political and cultural issues and which pushes for accountability and the ability of people to exercise their human rights. and three outcomes: Outcome 1: Wider media stakeholder/community are encouraged and enabled to produce ethical, inclusive and potentially viable public interest content that audiences trust and civic organisations use. Outcome 2: Journalists are safer online and have their rights protected in court and through documentation of press freedom violations. Outcome 3: Media support organizations and CO advocate successfully for laws that guarantee FoE and address disinformation and hate speech.

The overall objective of the intervention is to enhance partners and other stakeholders abilities to exercise their right to freedom of expression in a responsible, inclusive and diverse manner so that they can provide citizens with reliable public interest content and information (with a specific focus on East-Jerusalem, Area C, and the Gaza Strip).
Under this overarching objective there are three outcomes (pillars):
Outcome 1: Wider media stakeholders/community are encouraged and enabled to produce ethical, inclusive and potentially viable public interest content that audiences trust and civic organisations use.
Outcome 2: Media workers of all genders are better protected online and offline and enjoy safer working environments
Outcome 3: Media support organizations advocate for laws that guarantee freedom of expression and address disinformation and hate speech.

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution International Media Support 2022-2024

description.narrative:
During the reporting period, the programme continued progress in its three key pillars which also comprise the core of IMS overall strategy and theory of change: 1) public interest content, producing factual and impartial content that fulfils professional and ethical standards and is gender inclusive; 2) safety of journalists, supporting partners institutional development to enhance the safety of their journalists and employees at work; and 3) media enabling environment policy & law, which addresses the freedom of expression and safety-related aspects of the environments in which journalists and other content producers work.
It is important to note that this reporting period witnessed unprecedented political escalations that unfolded since October 2023. The current Israeli war on Gaza has led to a humanitarian catastrophe of historic proportions. The Israeli military's targeting of journalists and media workers has also resulted in an unprecedented number of casualties in the field.
IMS partners that contributed this year to the three pillars of the programme are: Nisaa FM (women-focused radio), Wattan TV (public interest TV station), Filmlab Palestine; Witness (young journalist organisation), Untold Palestine; the media unit at Mada Creative Center (MCC) in East Jerusalem; Filastiniyat (feminist media organisation) and the Gaza-based Community Development and Media Center (CDMC), 7amleh (The Arab Center for the Advancement of Social Media).
Some examples of results achieved under the different outcomes through different partners:
Nisaa FM continued to advocate for women's leadership across social, political, and economic spheres while highlighting womens rights and the barriers they face. Key topics included womens political participation, economic empowerment, the Family Protection Law, women with disabilities, and combating violence against women. Adapting to the evolving media landscape, Nisaa FM intensified efforts to digitize content, sharing podcasts, short videos, and testimonies from Gaza online. In total, 53 videos and reels were produced in 2023, amplifying womens voices and addressing critical issues.
CDMC conducted training sessions for 15 young journalists and multimedia graduates on podcast production and marketing. Four podcasts were produced, addressing topics such as gender discrimination and the role of NGOs in promoting positive community attitudes towards women. Moreover, CDMC compiled a cybercrime protection manual for women and youth in Gaza.
Filastiniyat conducted a comprehensive program of psychological counseling and well-being sessions for journalists in the West Bank and Gaza Strip. Moreover, NAWA; Filastiniyats online initiative for women journalists, produced 469 reports and stories in written and other multimedia formats, covering a wide range of topics. Moreover, journalists and media play an important role in documenting the war in Gaza and providing life-saving information to civilians. Since the beginning of the Gaza war, Filastiniyat was one of the first respondents providing emergency support for journalists. Filastiniyat took lead in coordinating the emergency response by setting up a task force of Palestinian organisations to coordinate support including human rights and womens rights organisations. The provided emergency support allowed journalists to continue working and the content produced have contributed to providing life-saving information to civilians in Gaza and raising the awareness internationally of the humanitarian crisis and needs.
Wattan TV produced and published a total of 180 stories for their TV and online audience. A good part of the stories published focused on gender and marginalized groups, people with disabilities and young women, as well as stories about women empowerment, women entrepreneurship, and women in elections. To cover the war on Gaza, Wattan produced and published daily stories across TV, radio, and online platforms featuring news coverage and expert guests to raise awareness of citizens' needs during the war. Additionally, Wattan launched the 'Voices from Gaza' program, which produced and published around 300 multimedia short stories in December 2023 about the humanitarian needs especially of children, women, people with disabilities, and other civilians affected by the attacks. Several published stories in the West Bank managed to create influence. For instance, a report by a Wattan TVs citizen journalist on the reconstruction and reopening of Al-Naim Bath in the old city of Hebron (one of the city's oldest Turkish baths) prompted action and led various parties to come together to restore it.
Yura/ Untold Palestine played a significant role in raising international awareness of Palestinian photography by holding two physical exhibitions in Berlin and Ramallah, featuring photo stories and highlighting Palestinian photographers.
The Center for Citizen Rights and Social Development (Witness), continued their platform project "From the Camp. The platform produced 70 content pieces in different formats covering refugee issues, including health infrastructure in Palestinian refugee camps.
Mada Creative Center (MCC) continued to document all forms of Israeli military and settler violations of international humanitarian and human rights law in East Jerusalem as well as violations of freedom of expression and attacks on journalists through video and live posting on social media platforms. MCC published 1465 videos, and 2-3 video reports and news videos per month.
Filmlab Palestine continued to develop Palestinian filmmakers capacities, support film production, and promote cinema and documentary as public interest content in Palestine. Filmlab Palestine supported the completion of two films in 2023, and facilitated six film productions through the only color grading studio in Palestine, which Filmlab established to enable Palestinian film productions to reduce their dependence on foreign donors.
On protection of media workers, and in order to respond to the growing and intensifying need of digital security knowledge and skills in particular given the situation, 7amleh has published a digital security emergency manual as well as a digital advocacy manual. Additionally, 7amleh has set up an emergency help desk for journalists, human rights defenders, and human rights organizations, which has been providing technical assistance, and so far has received 13 cases, and was accompanied by a social media campaign. 7amleh continued to document and address violations against Palestinian digital rights, publishing reports such as the annual #Hashtag Palestine report, reaching nearly 1.2 million people.
IMS partners managed to sustain and enhance their reach in 2023 despite restrictions on Palestinian content in the digital sphere. For example, Wattan managed to sustain its audience numbers, maintaining a significant reach of 47.6 million across all platforms. Witness experienced a notable increase in Facebook reach, soaring from 2.48 million in 2022 to 2.88 million in 2023, marking a substantial growth of 40,000. Yura/Untold Palestine saw a surge in its audience base, with over 120,000 new followers joining the platform and achieving a reach of over six million. MCC experienced an increase in followers and engagement on social media, with Facebook followers rising from 22.2K in 2022 to 22.5K in 2023, and Instagram followers increasing from 34.6K in 2022 to 53K in 2023.
